summary: Sh. Ali Mashhour discusses a hadith narration from Anas describing a marketplace in paradise that the people of paradise visit every Friday. He contrasts this with the marketplace in this life, which the Prophet describes as the furthest place from Allah due to lying, cheating, and deception. In paradise, a northern wind—symbolizing the best and most hopeful wind—blows through the marketplace and increases the beauty and adornment of the inhabitants. Sh. Ali Mashhour emphasizes that this weekly cycle of increasing beauty and luxury occurs eternally, meaning paradise continuously improves for eternity rather than remaining static. He explains that this eternal progression is essential because even an infinitely large but finite paradise would eventually become boring over infinite time.
suggested_title: The Marketplace of Paradise: Eternal Increase in Beauty and Bliss
